items.stem: What signals Oedipus' end?
options: The peals and flashes he reads as the gods' appointed warnings
An earthquake that has already opened a grave in the grove
A runner who has already arrived with news from a distant city
A dream he reports after waking beside the altar of the grove

items.stem: Whom does Oedipus call for?
options: Theseus
Creon
Polyneices
Teiresias

items.stem: Complete the line: “What doth the lightning-flash _____?”
options: portend
pardon
explain
conceal

items.stem: Complete the line: “Thy due _____. Haste, O King!”
options: guerdon
punishment
silence
ransom

items.stem: What does Time do, according to the Chorus?
options: Overthrows the great and raises the low
Stands still and leaves every fortune unchanged
Favors only kings and forgets everyone else
Erases the past so that no old deed can matter

items.stem: Why does Oedipus want the prince found while he is still “living” and his “senses clear”?
options: So the charge can be given while he can still speak it plainly
So the chorus can finish the sacrifice before night comes on now
So Antigone can ask him to turn back from the path at once
So Creon can be invited to share the gift he means to leave here

items.stem: What does the chorus ask of Zeus when the peals grow louder, if they have looked on a man of sin with pity?
options: Grace, not anger, for having looked with a pitying eye
A swift bolt to drive the stranger from the grove at once
A clear sign that the prince should refuse to come at all
A promise that no later warning will fall upon the land

items.stem: What ironic reversal is strange about Oedipus in this scene?
options: The blind man leads the others
He claims that his eyes have been fully restored
He sits down and will not take another step
He asks the chorus to carry him home at once

items.stem: Whom does Oedipus name as the spirit guide along the way he takes?
options: Hermes
Creon
Poseidon
Apollo

items.stem: Complete the line: “Daughters, upon me the _____ end”
options: forgotten
hidden
predestined
welcome

items.stem: Complete the line: “Would warrant all surmises of _____.”
options: victory
silence
mischance
honour

items.stem: Why does Oedipus say he would perform the promise made when he first received Theseus's benefits?
options: He means to keep, now, the pledge given when he was first received
He wants the chorus to take the prince's place at the altar
He hopes the daughters will be sent away before the prince arrives
He means to ask the prince to march at once against a neighbouring city

items.stem: How does Theseus first try to account for the general din as he arrives?
options: A thunderbolt of Zeus or a sleet of arrowy hail
A quarrel already settled between the daughters in the grove
A runner already sent from a neighbouring city with fresh terms
A sacrifice the chorus has already finished without him

items.stem: What does Oedipus refuse to reveal even to his own children, though he loves them dearly?
options: What Theseus must guard and whisper to his chosen heir alone
The names of the seven captains already waiting in the field
A plan to send the daughters home before the prince can speak
The words of a prayer the chorus has already finished at the altar

items.stem: What will protect Athens, according to Oedipus?
options: The secret of his resting place, passed to Theseus’ heir
A new stone wall built around the grove and the whole town
A sworn alliance with a neighbouring army for the coming year
A newly founded temple raised in the city's marketplace

items.stem: Complete the line: “The gods themselves are _____ of my fate;”
options: enemies
prisoners
servants
heralds

items.stem: Complete the line: “Thus shalt thou hold this land _____”
options: forgotten
conquered
deserted
inviolate

items.stem: What does Oedipus mean by “My life hath turned the scale”?
options: The appointed moment has arrived, and he means to act now
He has already left the grove and will not be found again
He has decided to refuse the prince any further gift or word
He believes the chorus can finish the matter without him

items.stem: Why does Oedipus say “Oh, touch me not, but let me all alone / Find out the sepulcher”?
options: He must find the place destiny appoints, going without a leading hand
He wants the daughters to go back and wait beside the altar alone now
He has already asked the chorus to hide the place from Theseus himself
He means to let the prince choose the place and mark it with a new wall

items.stem: Which literary element describes the turn by which the man long led now leads the seeing?
options: Irony
Comedy
Pathos
Allegory

items.stem: Complete the line: “Flash upon flash, from the _____ hand.”
options: unknown
unwilling
unburied
unconquered

items.stem: Complete the line: “Now the last time I feel thee _____,”
options: distant
forgotten
hidden
palpable

items.stem: Whom does Oedipus name as empress of the dead in this scene?
options: Persephassa
Lord Poseidon
Queen Antigone
King Aegeus

items.stem: What does Oedipus offer this state as a treasure age cannot corrupt?
options: A gift for Athens that he will unfold at the spot, to be guarded alone
A store of arms already gathered for the prince's men in the sacred grove
A written treaty already sealed with a neighbouring city's king
A new rite the chorus has already promised to sing each coming year

items.stem: How does Oedipus's warning about the dread Dragon’s brood and wanton neighbours function in the charge to Theseus?
options: It ties the just city's safety to the charge Theseus must keep, against future wrong
It tells us that a neighbouring army has already entered the grove this very hour
It asks Theseus to march at once and burn the fields beyond the far border
It claims that the daughters must be sent away before any gift can be given now

items.stem: How does Theseus's mind about the din change after he has heard Oedipus?
options: He first treats the din as a storm, then, trusting a true prophet, asks what must be done
He first dismisses the noise, then orders the chorus to leave the grove at once now
He first blames the daughters, then asks the chorus to finish the vow for him here
He first names a neighbouring city, then refuses to hear another word at all
